label: D1 after a rewarded a2->S2 (common) trial: win-stay on a2
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), only when the reward input is 1, and essentially only when the previous trial was a2 with a common transition to S2 (prev_common=0 or prev_action=1 carry ~0.2% of mass). On the window first trial the previous trial is not in the window, so that clause falls back to the agent own upcoming choice action==2 (a FUTURE variable but the agent own computed choice, which here is a win-stay repeat of a2); the purely observed version prev_action==2 & prev_state==2 & in_rew==1 has dev precision 0.88 but recall 0.75 only because of the missing first-trial history. Simpler (D1 & in_rew==1 & action==2) gives dev F1 0.86. Activation corresponds to a strongly a2-leaning policy (choice logit in [-4.4,-1.5] holds 93% of mass) and mid-high value. Does not fire after unrewarded trials, after a1 or rare trials, and is nearly silent in episode trials 90-99. False positives are mostly weaker/zero activations in long reward streaks or right after a S1R rare outcome earlier in the window.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: episode trials 90-99. On test, the original predicate restricted to ep_trial >= 90 predicts 10878 steps with precision 0.08 (dev 0.058). That accounts for roughly 10k of the predicate's ~15k dev false positives. The explanation says the feature is 'almost silent in episode trials 90-99' but leaves this out of the predicate. It also blames most false positives on 'late in long reward streaks', when the dominant cause is the late-episode cutoff.

Adding & (ep_trial < 90) raises test precision from 0.865 to 0.947, keeps recall at 0.969 and mass recall at 0.997, and lifts test F1 from 0.918 to 0.958 (dev 0.921 -> 0.963). So the reported predicate is not the best description, and the label is missing the late-episode suppression.

Confirmed claims: firing is D1-only (GO and D2 have 0 active steps). in_rew == 1 holds 100% of the mass. prev_action == 1 and prev_common == 0 each hold about 0.2% of the mass. The observed-only predicate scores dev P 0.876 / R 0.746, and its gap is entirely the window's first trial. Using good == 2 in place of action == 2 on the first trial drops the first-trial recall (0.175 vs 0.233). For the first trial, the future upcoming choice (action == 2) is a legitimate stand-in, since the agent computes it itself.
The policy correlation exists but is weaker than the predicate: D1 & in_rew == 1 & choice < -1 gives dev F1 0.878 and choice < -1.5 gives 0.845, so the policy logit alone is not a better explanation.
Residual false positives after the fix look scattered: first wins on a2 after unrewarded or switch trials, where activation is weak or zero. No further systematic class was found.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a rewarded a2->S2 (common) trial, i.e. win-stay on a2, except in the last ~10 trials of the episode (silent at ep_trial >= 90)
